# Good practice and next steps {#sec-m5-proximos-passos}

## What to take away from the course

If everything else is forgotten, let these six habits remain:

1. **Projects and relative paths.** No `setwd("C:/Users/...")`. It is what lets the
   script run on a colleague's machine.
2. **Raw data are never edited.** All cleaning happens in code, which makes it auditable
   and repeatable when the dataset is updated.
3. **Explicit checks.** `stopifnot()` wherever an assumption must hold, and
   row counts before and after each `join`.
4. **Investigate before discarding.** Both times ANTAQ's data looked wrong, the
   investigation revealed structure: an extra dimension and a legitimate category (@sec-m1-limpeza).
5. **State your choices.** CRS, classification method, grade limit, correction factor,
   departure time: everything that changes the result must be written down.
6. **The report is code.** If it does not render from scratch, it is not ready.

## Mistakes that keep coming back

| Symptom | Likely cause |
|:--|:--|
| "The layers don't overlap" | different CRS: `st_transform()`, never `st_set_crs()` |
| *Buffer* with an odd shape or an absurd area | metric operation on geographic coordinates |
| The report's total doubled | `join` with a duplicated key on the right-hand side |
| A numeric column became text | decimal separator, `-` or `n/d` instead of `NA` |
| The chart came out empty | `NA` introduced by silent conversion |
| Tracts "with no population" | municipality name spelt differently in the other dataset |
| `Inf` in routing | points in disconnected components of the network |
| The map lost flow | pairs without a coordinate; check the sum before and after |

## How to keep learning

**Everyday reference**

- [R for Data Science (2nd ed.)](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/): wrangling and visualisation.
- [Geocomputation with R](https://r.geocompx.org/): the reference book for spatial analysis.
- [Introduction to urban accessibility with R](https://ipeagit.github.io/intro_access_book/):
  from the group that makes `r5r` and `aopdata`.
- The [*cheat sheets*](https://posit.co/resources/cheatsheets/) for `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, `sf` and
  Quarto, printed and next to the keyboard.

**Communities**

- Packages' *issues* sections: that is where the authors answer, and where the real problems are.
- [R-bloggers](https://www.r-bloggers.com/) and the [Posit Community](https://forum.posit.co/) forum.
- The [ipeaGIT](https://github.com/ipeaGIT) ecosystem, which maintains `geobr`, `censobr`, `r5r`,
  `aopdata`, `gtfstools` and `geocodebr`. It is worth following the releases.

**Natural next topics for this team**

| Topic | Where to start |
|:--|:--|
| Demand models (generation, distribution, mode choice) | `mlogit`, `apollo` |
| Spatial regression | `spatialreg`, `GWmodel` |
| Time series and forecasting | `fable`, `forecast` |
| Interactive dashboards | `shiny`, `flexdashboard`, `mapgl` |
| Automating routines and APIs | `httr2`, `targets`, GitHub Actions |
| Large volumes | `arrow`, `duckdb`, `sfarrow` |

The `targets` package deserves a special mention: it organises long analyses as a
chain of steps, rerunning only what changed. It is the natural next step once a
project's script goes past a few hundred lines.

## Keeping the material alive

This site remains available after the course and can receive additions: new case studies,
corrections and code the team itself develops. Contributions are welcome through the
repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Joaobazzo/curso-r-transportes.git
cd curso-r-transportes
quarto preview
```

Corrections and suggestions through the
[*issues*](https://github.com/Joaobazzo/curso-r-transportes/issues), including typos,
which are the easiest to fix and the most useful for whoever comes next.

## Closing

The goal of the course was never to teach a language, but to change the way work is done: moving from
analyses that exist once, inside a spreadsheet, to analyses that are recorded,
can be audited, corrected and rerun when the data change.

If, at the end, a routine that today takes a day comes to take ten minutes, and can be repeated
by any colleague on the team, the course has done what it set out to do.
